article.title: Chip Huyen explains how to cut inference costs without new hardware
article.summary: Last October, the P99 conference — the online gathering for developers focused on high-performance, low-latency applications — featured a cracking keynote from Chip Huyen.  The author of the best-selling AI Engineering , Huyen opened with simple math: Training a frontier model is a one-off cost, but inference is the same cost paid over and over. That’s great for the frontier model providers, and bad for us token burners. Over the life of a model, Huyen reckons the compute split ratio lands somewhere between 1:10 and 1:100 for training to inference. Reasoning models — which burn even more tokens — push that out even further. We all know the feeling of hitting our weekly session quotas. article.title: Lenovo Googlebook 15 specs leak, and this clearly isn’t your schoolhouse Chromebook
article.summary: TL;DR Lenovo’s upcoming Googlebook 15 has reportedly leaked in full, revealing a 15.3-inch 120Hz OLED display, Intel Core Ultra 5 325 chip, and up to 32GB of RAM. The laptop could also feature a 70Wh battery, Wi-Fi 7, dual Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, a fingerprint reader, and a Google-colored battery/charging light on the lid. Googlebook OS will put Gemini Intelligence and Android phone integration front and center, while Lenovo is also preparing a dedicated Google key and an “AI Mouse” accessory. Earlier in May this year, Google introduced its Googlebook laptop category. These are laptops designed from the ground up for Gemini Intelligence, with Google aiming to create a PC experience that offers premium hardware, works seamlessly with Android phones, and puts AI features front and center.

article.title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to ‘distill’ frontier models, too
article.summary: Tan wants smaller, American open-weight AI labs to use the same kind of training techniques on American frontier AI labs, giving the U.S. a more robust set of open-weight options that aren’t Chinese.

article.title: Nvidia Mulls $10 Billion Anthropic IPO Backing, Reuters Says
article.summary: Nvidia Corp. is considering investing as much as $10 billion in Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering, which could become the biggest IPO of all time, Reuters reported.

article.title: China’s Data Regulator Plans Standards Push for Embodied AI
article.summary: China’s data regulator said it plans to develop standards for embodied artificial intelligence and guide local authorities in related work, as demand for high-quality, diverse and large-scale datasets continues to grow.

article.title: Anthropic’s AI Warning May Weigh on Chips, But Trade Seen Intact
article.summary: AI executives’ calls to slow development of the technology are likely to weigh on chipmaker and supply-chain stocks in the near term, but will probably have limited long-term impact as spending on computing infrastructure remains strong, market watchers say.
